hero.label: First day with clark
hero.title: Keep the record. Shape the report. Publish it.
hero.lead: In clark you keep one project record of work items, milestones and use cases, shape the weekly report from it, and publish the report as a web page (and a Word document if you like) for the client. Every change to the record and the report saves on its own and can be undone. Publishing and restoring a published report cannot be undone.

loop.d: Import from Excel: actions, risks and issues, decisions, milestones and use cases. Or add them by hand with the **+** buttons.
On Work items and Milestones, open anything in the peek and change it where it is.
On the Dashboard, press **Edit**. Write the current state, set the health and choose what the client sees.
Use ask clark to **Check this report**. It reads the project’s data and says what looks wrong.
Publish from the profile circle. Local is always saved; the client folder only when you tick **To client**.

first.d: In [Settings › Profile](go:settings#profile), fill in your name. It goes on every change you make.
The project name in the top bar switches projects.
On [Work items](go:work), press the import icon. **Get the template** gives you a workbook with the right columns.
In [Settings › Publishing](go:settings), set a local folder and, if the client has one, their SharePoint folder.
**Preview the page in a new tab**, in the profile circle menu, shows exactly what the client will see. Nothing is saved.

jobs: Put a new task on the plan and say who owns it.
Fill in the status, the highlights and the next steps.
Add a section from a template
Start a new section from a ready-made layout.
Change the order of the report, or take parts out.
Check the report, then send the finished copy.
where: The weekly report itself. **View** shows it as the client will read it; **Edit** changes it in place.
Every action, risk, issue and decision, as a table or a board, with filters and search.
**Plan** shows every milestone on a timeline or calendar; **Movement** shows slippage, for you and the team only.
Each row shows the reference, the name, where it stands, the status, the open work items, the milestones and whether it is on the dashboard.
Answers questions about the project and checks the report. Press [[/]], or open the palette with [[Mod+K]] and choose ask clark.
Publish, Preview, Export to Excel, Export to Word, Import from Word, Published reports, Appearance (System, Light or Dark), Settings and Help. At the top right.
Your profile and look, projects, source folders, publishing, data, version and updates, and diagnostics.
rules: Every change saves on its own
There is no Save button. A change is kept as you make it, and the message at the foot of the page offers **Undo**.
Only what you show is published
Items, sections, tiles and documents you leave out are dropped from the published file, not hidden inside it.
Publishing saves files. The client folder is used only when you tick **To client**. Nothing is ever emailed.
It works from this project’s data and the source folders you list, never mail, Teams or calendars. What it changes can be undone.

text.loop_intro: Every week follows the same five steps.
text.loop_return: Next week starts the loop again from the same record. The history keeps every change, so nothing is lost between weeks.
text.keyline: ask: the speech-bubble button in the top bar, or press [[/]] · [[/]] [[/]] Sneak peek, with a work item open in Edit · [[Esc]] close the top thing · [[Mod+Enter]] keep an edit · [[?]] Help
text.foot_link: How do I…: step by step for every job
text.jobs_lead: Pick a job and follow the steps. Each one is short.

s: Open the **Dashboard** and press **Edit** at the top. Each change saves on its own.

Set **Week ending** to the Friday the report covers: type it as DD-MM-YYYY, press [[Enter]] in the box to use the Friday shown (only while no week is kept yet), or press the calendar button beside the box and pick the day. In the calendar, **Friday** takes the next Friday (today, if it is one). Any other day is not accepted.

Click the text under **Current state** and write where the project stands. It turns into an editor where it is: there is no Save button. Click away or press [[Mod+Enter]] to keep it; [[Esc]] puts the old text back. Write the Summary, This week and Next week sections the same way.
Set the health on the **Project health** tile: see [Set the project health](#howto-set-the-health).
Check the lists of risks and issues, open actions and decisions. Click any part of a row (the state, the title, the owner, the date) to change it there; the ID opens the whole item in the peek.
Press **View** to read the report as the client will.
In Edit, press the health pill on the **Project health** tile and choose **On track**, **At risk** or **Off track**.
Write why in the box beside it, in a line or two. It saves when you leave the box; [[Esc]] puts the old reason back.
A change of health needs a reason: without one, nothing is changed.
The tile takes the health’s colour.

tasks.t: Check the report with ask clark
s: Press [[/]] when you aren’t typing in a box and no peek, menu or box is open, or press [[Mod+K]] and choose **ask clark**. It opens down the right-hand side.
Press **Check this report**. It reads the project’s data and says what looks wrong.

An answer may suggest a change to a work item or a milestone as a card that shows it now and as it would be. Nothing is saved until you press **Apply**; **Undo** takes it back. If the change came from one of your files, you tick a box first.

Ask anything else in your own words, or press a suggestion: **What is overdue?**, **Which risks are red?**, **What is the next milestone?**, **Summarise this week** or **Which use cases need attention?**.
**New chat** at the top starts again. **Close**, [[Esc]] or a click outside closes the panel. Drag its left edge to make it wider.
Press your profile circle at the top right and choose **Publish…**.

**Local** is always ticked: the save window opens where you last saved for this project, and you choose the folder and the name. Tick **To client** to send it to the client folder set in Settings as well. With no folder set, the box is off and says so.

Tick **Also a Word document** for a Word copy in the folder last used for this project. If a Word file with that name is already in the folder, you are asked whether to add a number or replace it. A copy already in the client folder is never replaced: the new one gets a number. Tick **Also a PDF** for the page as it prints: your browser’s print box opens, and you choose Save as PDF.

With **To client** ticked, a line says the client will see the page, and the Word report if you ticked it, and only what is shown in View mode. If a work item shown to the client still has its placeholder title, the box warns you; it does not stop you, so rename the item or turn off its eye first.

Press **Publish locally** (or **Publish and send to the client**). The button shows a spinner while it works, then a green tick and, for example, “Published (Publication 3)”. The box closes by itself after a moment; you can press the button to close it at once. If the file name is taken, the box asks what to do: Add a number, Rename it or, where it is allowed, Overwrite the existing file.
To look first, choose **Preview the page in a new tab** in the same menu. Nothing is saved.
tasks.n: The file is named after the project’s short code and the week ending date, for example “DPP-report-2026-10-30.html”. Each publish, a local one too, gets the project’s next number (Publication 1, 2, 3 and so on). A number is never used again, and **Undo** does not take it back. The line at the top of the Dashboard says when it was last published, and whether to the client or locally.

tasks.t: Export to Word, or bring items in from a Word file
tasks.w: Profile circle › Export to Word · Import from Word
s: Press your profile circle and choose **Export to Word**. The report is saved as a Word file in the folder last used for this project; if there is none yet, a window asks you to choose one. Tick **To client** to copy it to the client folder as well (you can tick it once a client folder is saved in Settings › Publishing).

If a file with that name is already there, you are asked: **Add a number** (keeps the old file and saves the new one beside it), **Replace it** (it asks you to confirm) or **Cancel**. Nothing is saved until you choose.
In **Publish**, tick **Also a Word document** to save a Word copy of the report with it.

Choose **Import from Word** from the same menu, choose a .docx file of up to 25 MB and press **Read the file**. Work items under a heading called Actions, Risks, Issues or Decisions are listed. Tick the ones you want, or use **Tick all**, and press the Add button, which reads **Add** and the number you ticked, such as Add 3 items. Nothing is added until you press it. The new items are shown to the client until you hide them with the eye, and Undo takes them all back.
If clark refuses a file it says why in plain words and names the file. Choose the same file again once you have fixed it: **Read the file** comes on again.
tasks.n: The use case table in the Word report has a Commitment column.

tasks.t: Find or open a past publication
s: Press your profile circle and choose **Published reports**, or go to Settings and find the **Published reports** card for the open project.
Each row has the publication's number, the date and time, where it went and who published it. The newest is first, and the card lists the latest ten.
Press **Open** to see the kept copy of the page in a new tab, as it was published. A row that says **Not kept** has no copy to open.
**Archive** on a row takes the publication out of the list. **Show archived** lists the archived ones, each with **Restore**. Times are shown as UTC.

tasks.t: Save the report as a PDF
s: Open the Publish box and tick **Also a PDF**. It needs nothing on the computer but your browser.
Press **Publish locally** (or **Publish and send to the client**). The web page is saved as usual, and your browser’s print box opens on the page in a new tab.
In the print box, choose **Save as PDF**. Under More settings, untick Headers and footers, so the PDF carries no web address and no date from the browser.
The PDF has the tabs one after another, with Use cases last, no buttons or menus, and the publication number, the date and the page number at the foot of each page.
tasks.n: The PDF is made by your browser, not by clark, and it is not kept or copied to the client folder, so save it where you want it. If the print box does not open, allow pop-ups for this page. Checked in Google Chrome; another browser may print the page without the publication line at the foot.

tasks.w: Work items › the + at the top right
s: On **Work items**, press the **+** at the top right. Point at it and it shows what it adds, following the type switch: **Add action**, **Add decision**, **Add risk or issue** (a menu of Risk and Issue) and, on All, **Add item** (a menu of Action, Risk, Issue and Decision). You can do this in View as well as in Edit.
The new item is made at once and opens in the peek with its title selected: type over it. A message at the foot of the page says it was added, with **Undo**.
Its due date (a week from today; a decision’s needed-by date is today), and an action’s priority, are placeholders. Change them in the list or in the peek.
A new item is shown to the client to start with. While one still has its placeholder title, the Publish box warns you. Rename it, or turn off its eye, before you publish.
In Edit on the Dashboard, the last row of each list adds one too: type “Owner: what it is” (the owner, a colon, then what it is) and press [[Enter]].
The first switch picks the type: **All**, **Actions**, **Risks and issues** or **Decisions**.
The second picks **Open**, **Closed** or **All**, each with its count.

Click the filter line, which says **Filter by keyword or by field**, and type. A plain word finds the items with it in the title or the ID. A list of fields and values opens under the line: choose from it, or keep typing.

To pick a field, type field:value, for example status:Open or priority:High,Urgent. The fields are type, status, owner, priority, due, workstream, usecase, milestone, client and is. A comma means or, a space between two parts means and, and a - in front means not, as in -status:Closed. no:owner finds the items with no owner, has:owner the items with one, and owner:@me means you (set your name in Settings first).

A word it cannot use gets a red wavy underline and is not applied. A message under the line says why, such as There is no “x” filter. or Add a value after 'x:'. If you ask for owner:@me before your name is set, it says Set your name in Settings to see your actions.

The count at the right reads, for example, 12 of 40. **Clear filter** (the **×**) empties the line. When nothing matches the words you typed, the list says, for example, No open items match "crane". and offers **Clear search**.

A published file has no filter line. It has a **Search work items** box, which finds words in the ID, the description, the owner, the latest update, the client wording and the use case, and a **Filter by** row with Workstream, Status, Due, Owner, Priority, Use case and Milestone. Each opens a list with a count beside every value: tick the ones you want and choose **is any of** or **is not**. **Select all** and **Clear** are at the top. The filters that are on show as chips beside the count; **×** on a chip removes it, and **Clear all** removes the filters and the search but keeps the type and Open, Closed or All.

Your choices are kept for next time. A tile on the Dashboard, or the **See all** button on a use case (it reads “See all N work items” and the use case's reference), opens Work items already filtered to what it counts.

tasks.t: Group work and use the board
s: The **View** menu beside the saved views holds the grouping. **Group by** chooses the groups: Workstream, Status, Due, Owner, Priority, Milestone, Type, or Nothing (the table only). In the table, a group’s heading collapses it, and clark remembers.
The two icons beside the View menu, **Table** and **Board**, switch between the table and the board. The board’s columns follow Group by (Status when it is Nothing).
On the board, **Swimlanes** in the View menu adds rows across it: No lanes, Workstream lanes or Type lanes.

Drag a card to another column to change that field. **Due** asks for the new date (never a past one); **Overdue** isn’t a place to drop; **No date** clears it. A move across a lane and a column changes both in one step.
From the keyboard, or for a precise move, press the three-dots button on a card and choose from **Move to…**: the columns, then the lanes.
Press a column’s heading to collapse it, and again to open it. The full-screen icon gives the board the whole window; [[Esc]] leaves it.
Every move has **Undo** in the message. Click a card, or press [[Enter]] on it, to open it.
tasks.n: A move that doesn’t fit says so: an action can’t be Made, and nothing changes its type by moving.

tasks.t: Change an item in the peek
tasks.w: Any work item: a row or a card
s: Click a row or a card, or press [[Enter]] on it. The item opens in the **peek** at the right, and the page stays where it was.
Click the title to change it. [[Enter]] keeps it; [[Esc]] puts it back.

Under the title are **Status**, **Priority**, **Owner** and **Due**. Click one to choose another value. A risk’s or issue’s status menu also sets its colour (Red, Amber or Green), which sets its priority. The due date offers Today, Tomorrow, Friday, Next week and No date.
A warning shows when an action is overdue or due on a weekend, with one-click fixes such as **Move to Friday**.
**Needed from the client**: switch it on in Edit and the item is listed under “Needs from you”.
**Latest update**: click to write it. **Draft** writes one from the item’s own facts. On an item shown to the client, the box says **Shown to the client**, because the client sees this text.
**Details** holds the description, type, workstream, milestone, use case and client wording. It stays open or closed as you last left it.
In Edit, the **Activity** tab under the title shows the item’s history: who changed what, how and when, newest first. **Details** goes back to the fields.
With the peek open, click another item anywhere on the page and the peek moves to it. A click elsewhere, or [[Esc]], closes it. The up and down arrows at the top step through the list.
tasks.n: Drag the peek’s left edge to make it wider (a double-click puts it back), or press the corners icon to take it across the whole screen. Your width is kept.

tasks.t: Change an item with words (Sneak peek)
tasks.w: A work item open in Edit › [[/]] [[/]]
s: With a work item open in the peek in Edit, press [[/]] twice quickly (when you aren’t typing in a box).
Type the change, for example “move to Friday, owner Jo, high priority”.
Under the box, the words you typed are shown in the order you typed them, then a line for each field shows what it is now and what it will become.

Press **Make the change** or [[Enter]] to make every change shown, in one step ([[Shift+Enter]] makes them and keeps the box open). **Not now** or [[Esc]] closes the box. The fields that changed flash for a moment, and the message has **Undo**.

Closing an item, making or withdrawing a decision, marking a milestone Achieved or a use case Done asks first: press **Confirm and apply**, [[Mod+Enter]] or **Make the change** (the words and the lines are on screen above it). A decision that is made cannot be undone from here.
tasks.n: If the owner is not already named in the project, the line is marked “new name”. See [Sneak peek](#ref-sneak-peek) for what it understands.

tasks.w: Work items · the peek · Dashboard › Edit
s: On Work items, the eye in each row’s last column turns client-visible on or off. In the peek, it is the eye at the top.
On the Dashboard in Edit, the eye beside a row takes it off the page. The row greys while **Undo** is offered, then leaves.
**+ Add from your project record** under a list brings items back. A picker opens: search, choose a kind, tick what you want (or **Select all shown**) and press **Add**.
Milestones, use cases, supporting documents and tiles have their own eye and their own **Add back**. A whole section is left out from its options: **Leave out of the published page**.
An item’s **Client wording** (in the peek’s Details) is used on the page in place of its title. A milestone has the same, under **Client view**.
tasks.n: The report’s lists show only client-visible items. Everything else is left out of the published file altogether.

tasks.w: Work items toolbar · Settings › Data · profile circle
s: **Export**: press the down-arrow icon. You get one workbook with a sheet each for Actions, Risks & Issues, Decisions, Milestones and Use cases, and a Gantt sheet when the project has Gantt lines, named after today and the project.
**Import**: press the up-arrow icon. The box lists the sheets and columns it reads. **Get the template** downloads a workbook with the right columns.

Press **Choose a file** (an Excel .xlsx workbook). The box **What to import** lists the sheets the workbook has, the Gantt sheet after the others, each with its rows and all ticked: untick any you do not want, then press **Continue**. **Check the import** then shows how many rows are new, updated or skipped, and the first few; press **Import** to save them.
A row with an ID that exists updates that item; a row without one adds a new item. Only the title or name is needed. A new workstream is added to the project.
tasks.n: The whole import is one step: one **Undo** takes it all back.

s: In Edit, each section has a control at the left of its card (in the margin on a wide window, inside the card on a narrow one): a move button and, under it, a **+**. They are faint until you point at the section or tab to them.
Drag the move button to move the section, or focus it and press [[Alt+Up]] or [[Alt+Down]]. Click it, or press [[Enter]] or [[Space]] on it, to open the section’s menu.

The menu has **Add a template below…**, then **Template settings** (for a section whose template has settings), **Move up** and **Move down**, **Place beside the next section** (or **Full width** when it is already beside another), then **Leave out of the published page** (or **Include in the published page**) and **Delete section**. A section that is left out shows a small eye mark under its **+** and the tag **Left out of the published page**.

To rearrange the page, pick up a section by its move button and drop it. A line between rows puts it on a row of its own; the left or right half of a section that is on its own puts the two side by side, half the width each. A row never holds more than two. The cover stays at the top. Each drop is one step you can undo, and on a narrow window a pair stacks.
Click a heading to rename it. [[Enter]] keeps it; [[Esc]] puts it back.
A section left out stays in Edit, greyed, and disappears in View and on the published page.

tasks.t: Add a section from a template
tasks.w: Dashboard › Edit › the + under a section’s move button
s: On the **Dashboard**, press **Edit**. Press the **+** under the move button of the section you want the new one to follow, or open its menu and choose **Add a template below…**.

The **Add a section** box opens. Choose a kind on the left, or type in **Search templates**. [[Left]], [[Right]], [[Up]] and [[Down]] move through the templates; the preview on the right shows what the chosen one holds.

Under **Where it goes**, choose **On its own row** or, when the section above is on a row of its own and the template can be half width, **Beside** it: the new section becomes the second half of that row.
Press **Add section** (or [[Enter]]). The new section appears with its heading ready to rename; [[Esc]] closes the box without adding anything.
The new section opens ready to fill in, in place. A template with nothing in it yet is left out of what the client sees.
One **Undo** takes the new section away again. See [Section templates](#ref-section-templates) for what each one is for.

tasks.t: Ask the client for what you need
s: On the **Dashboard**, press **Edit**. Add a section from the **Needs from you** template: press the **+** under the section you want it to follow, choose **Needs from you** and press **Add section**.
Press **Add a row**. Choose whether it is a decision, information or a date. Say what is needed and who it is from, then write the day it is needed by as DD-MM-YYYY, or leave it empty. Press **Add**.
Each row has **Edit**, **Leave out** (or **Include**) and **Remove**. A row you leave out stays in Edit and is not shown in View or on the published page.
A date that has passed shows the word **Overdue** beside it. In View and on the published page the section is a table you can read but not change.
Each row you add, change, leave out or remove is one change with its own **Undo**.
On the **Dashboard**, press **Edit**. In a **Progress tracker** section, press **Add a group**, give it a name and press **Add**. A group holds the plan lines for one part of the work.

In a group, press **Add a line**. Give it a number if you like, say what it is, and pick its **Status**: Planned, In progress, Completed or Late. Type its **Weight**, what was **Planned** and what was **Achieved** as percentages, and its start and end as DD-MM-YYYY. Weight is how much of the whole plan the line is worth. Across all the lines, the weights, the Planned figures and the Achieved figures can each add up to 100% at most. Press **Add**.
Each line has **Edit**, the arrows to move it up or down, and **Remove**. A group has **Rename**, the arrows and **Remove group**.

The figures at the top are worked out for you: Achieved and Planned are the totals of all the lines. A line, a group or the whole that is behind plan shows ▼ and how many points behind. If the weights do not add up to 100%, a note under the section in Edit says so. Change a weight to fix it.

Under the bar is a status and a line of words. Unless you pick the **Health** yourself (On track, At risk or Off track), the status is set for you: On track when the work is ahead of plan or no more than 2 points behind it, At risk from there up to 9.9 points behind, and Off track from 10 points behind. The words say how far behind or ahead of plan you are. Click the words to write your own: they stop at one line when the section is full width and three lines when it sits beside another. Press **Use the automatic words** to go back. Switch on the Tasks, Agents or Workflows columns if you want them. Each of those columns holds a count you type for every line. In View and on the published page the section can be read but not changed.

To change how big the section is, press the cog on it, or press the grip and choose **Template settings**. Choose Large, Medium, Small or Compact. The choice applies to this section only, and the published page shows the same size.
Each line, group or setting you change is one change with its own **Undo**.

tasks.t: Use the At a glance tiles
s: Next to **Project health** are the counts: **Overdue actions**, **High risks and issues** and **Decisions needed** (hidden to start with).
Click a count, or press [[Enter]] on it, to open Work items filtered to exactly what it counts.
In Edit, drag a tile to reorder it, or press [[Alt+Left]] or [[Alt+Right]]. The eye hides a tile: it is left out of the published page.
Right-click a tile in Edit for **Outline colour**: **Automatic, from the data**, Green, Amber, Red or **No colour**.
tasks.n: The colour is a thin outline that fades from the bottom-left corner. Automatic is red when an action is overdue or an open risk or issue is rated Urgent or High, amber when something waits, and green otherwise.

s: The section opens with a strip: how many use cases, a count for each status and a small meter. Then one slim row each: the ID, the name, the headline, the status and the open next steps.

Click a row (or press [[Enter]] or [[Space]]) to open its detail in place: **Where it stands** and **Next steps**. The **See all** button, which reads “See all N work items” and the use case's reference, counts every linked item, open or closed, and opens Work items filtered to that use case.
In Edit, click the headline or the name to change it; click the status word to choose **On track**, **Flag**, **High risk** or **Done**.

A use case can carry a commitment: Candidate, Committed or Planned 2027. It shows as a small chip beside the status on the Dashboard, on the Use cases page and on the published page, and nothing shows when there is none.
In Edit, a small menu beside the status reads **Set commitment** when there is none: choose a word, or **No flag** to clear it. Each choice is one change, with one Undo and one line in History.
A published file shows the chip but never the menu. A use case taken off the page with the eye is left out of the published file whole, chip and all.
In the detail, write **Where it stands**, or add a next step as “Owner: what it is”.
**Archive this use case** asks first. It leaves the usual lists, the counts and the published page; its work items stay and lose the link. **Restore** or Undo brings it back.

tasks.t: Find and open a use case
s: Open the **Use cases** tab. Each row shows the reference, the name, where it stands, the status, the open work items, the milestones and whether it is on the dashboard. A use case with a commitment shows it as a small chip beside the status.
Type in **Search use cases** to narrow the list, or use **Status** and the **On the dashboard** and **Not on the dashboard** buttons. **Clear the filters** puts them all back.
Change the order with **Sort**: **Reference**, **Status** or **Open work items**.

Click a name to open the use case on its own page. The **Use cases** link at the top, [[Esc]] or the Back button of your browser brings you back to the list. The small menu beside the status there reads **Set commitment**: choose a word, or **No flag**. Each choice is one change, with one Undo and one line in History.
In Edit, press **+ Add a document link** at the foot of the report.
Give it a title, a kind (Minutes, Actions list, Report, Slides, Plan or Other), the link and a date, then press **Add**.
**⋯** on a document edits or removes it. The eye takes it off the page; **+ Add back a document** brings it back.
In View, and on the published page, the title and the arrow open the document in a new tab.
**Personal › Dashboard sections** is yours alone: **Slim gaps**, **Roomy gaps**, **Grey headers** or **One card** (the standard).

**Personal › Appearance** is **Light**, **Dark** or **System**. System is the standard: it follows your Mac’s setting and changes when the Mac does. **Appearance** in the profile circle menu has the same three: System, Light and Dark.

Personal › Keys has Single-key shortcuts, on as standard. Turn it off and the letter keys (V, E and the others) do nothing when pressed alone on the page. Arrows, Enter, Esc, Space and Ctrl or Cmd keys still work.
On **Milestones**, press **+** (**Add milestone**). A new one, called New milestone and agreed 30 days out, opens in the peek. There is no **+** in a published file.
Click any milestone to open it: its mark or label on the timeline, its chip on the calendar, or its row in the details.
**State**: Forecast, On track, At risk, Slipped or Achieved. Overdue follows the dates and can’t be picked. The line under it says why the milestone has that state.
**Dates**: the **Agreed** date is the baseline; change the **Forecast** date as things move. When they differ, **Rebaseline…** makes the forecast the new agreed date and keeps the original.
**Progress** is set by hand with the slider or the number. Add a **Description**, the **Owner** and the **Workstream**.
**Client view**: **Visible to client**, and the **Client wording** used on the page in place of the name.
**Linked work items** lists the items tied to it. Link one from the item’s peek, under Details, Milestone.
The **Timeline** scrolls sideways. The arrows move along it and **Today** comes back. Drag its bottom edge to zoom in or out; **Reset** puts it back.
A slipped milestone keeps its mark on the agreed date, with a dashed ring where it is now expected and a dashed line between them.
The two buttons at the top right, **Timeline** and **Calendar**, switch between them. Your choice is kept.
The calendar shows **Week**, **Month** (the standard) or **Quarter**, with the arrows and **Today**. In Quarter, click a month’s name to open that month.

With the keyboard, [[Tab]] reaches the calendar once, on today (or the first day when today is not shown). [[Left]] and [[Right]] move a day at a time, and [[Up]] and [[Down]] a week. [[Enter]] on a day with milestones goes to the first of them, and [[Shift+Tab]] or [[Esc]] comes back to the day.
**Legend**, at the right under the milestones, explains every mark when you point at it or tab to it.

Under the Legend, the list shows each milestone with its date, state and progress. The first five show; **Show all** shows the rest. **Hide milestone details** folds the list away and **Show milestone details** brings it back. Your choice is kept.
tasks.n: On the published page, Slipped reads “Expected later” and Overdue reads “Late”.

s: On **Milestones**, use the **Movement** switch next to **Plan** at the top. It is for you and the team: it is never published.
The first line says how many open milestones are behind their agreed date. The line under it names the one furthest behind.

Each open milestone has a row, the furthest behind first: its state, its agreed date, a small bar with a mark for the agreed date, one for the forecast and one for today, how far after the agreed date it is, and how often the agreed date has moved. Click a row, or move between rows with [[Up]] and [[Down]] and press [[Enter]], to choose it.
Its card shows the original, agreed and forecast dates, its progress and its owner, then **What changed**: each change, with who made it and when.

Under **Decide what to do**, choose **Hold: keep the forecast, agreed date unchanged**, or **Move the agreed date**. A move asks for **New agreed date (DD-MM-YYYY)**, **Who agreed it**, a **Reason** and a **Source**, and says what will happen before you press **Move the agreed date**. **Keep the date** closes it with no change. A milestone that has not slipped cannot be moved.
**Hold** and **Move the agreed date** each change the record at once, and each has its own **Undo**. A move keeps the original date and records a decision.

tasks.t: Add a recovery action, escalate or write a note on a slipped milestone
s: On **Milestones**, press **Movement**. It is for you and the team: it is never published.
Click a row to choose it. Its card shows the dates, how often it moved, and **What changed**.

Then decide: **Hold** (adds a dated line to the **Internal note** and keeps the agreed date), **Move the agreed date** (you say who agreed it, why and where; the original date is kept), **Add a recovery action** (a High priority action due in 7 days, linked to the milestone, in its workstream or the first open one) or **Escalate to steering** (a Pending decision needed in 7 days, named for the milestone: a decision can’t be linked to a milestone). Each new item opens in the peek, with a line saying how far behind the milestone is. A new item starts hidden from the client (its eye is off), so neither it nor that line reaches the client until you show it.
Write an **Internal note**. It saves when you leave the box and is never published.

Click the text. An editor opens where it is, with a bar of headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, lists, a checklist, indent and outdent, a quote, a divider, Link, Unlink, Clear, undo and redo, and **✦ AI**.
Highlight some words and a small bar floats above them, with the same formatting and the AI menu.

Type [[/]] at the start of a line or after a space for the command menu: Text, Heading 1 to 3, lists, a checklist, a quote, a divider and the AI options. Type to narrow it; [[Up]] and [[Down]] move, [[Enter]] inserts, [[Esc]] closes.
Click away, or press [[Mod+Enter]], to keep the text. [[Esc]] cancels the edit.
tasks.n: Titles, headings and table cells are plain text: [[Enter]] keeps the change and [[Esc]] puts it back.

s: Select some words. The floating bar has an AI part: **Format notes** (when you select two or more lines of a report section), **Improve**, **Structure**, **Make into** and **Ask…**.
Or press **✦ AI** on the editor’s bar for every option at once, on the selection or on the whole text. Where the field allows it, **Draft from the project** is first.

**Improve**: Rewrite clearly, Shorter, Longer, Make it executive and Polish. **Structure**: Add headings and bold, Pull out the tasks and Summarise at the top. **Make into**: a new action, risk or decision from the text. **Ask…**: say what you want in your own words.
The answer is a suggestion: your text is unchanged until you press **Accept**. **Show changes** marks what goes and what comes, word by word. **Try again** asks again; **Discard** ([[Esc]]) drops it.
After you accept, the editor’s undo ([[Mod+Z]]) takes it back.
tasks.n: Item fields and client wording offer Improve and Ask; report sections offer Structure and Format notes as well.

s: In **Settings › Projects**, press **+** (**Add project**). Give it a name, a short code (3 to 7 letters or digits, suggested from the name; it can’t change later), the client and its workstreams, separated by commas.
A new project opens on Work items, ready for an import.

Each project has **Open**, **Edit** and **Archive**. Archive hides the project and everything in it from the usual lists, the counts and the published page; **Show archived** finds it, and **Restore** and **Undo** bring it back.
Under the projects, set this project’s **Publishing** folders. The folders ask clark may read are in the **Asking** card, under **Folders asking may read**.
The project name in the top bar switches projects, shows each one’s open items, and has **Project settings**.
In **Settings**, find the **AI** card. It shows Claude and ChatGPT, each as **Connected** or **Not connected**.

Press **Connect** under the one you use if it says **Not connected**. No password is asked for: the Claude or ChatGPT command already signed in on this computer is the one used. If it is not signed in, the card says what to do.
Connect Claude or ChatGPT for ask clark: the passages it sends leave this computer, go to the one you choose and count against that plan. No password or key is kept.
Choose the model in **Model for ask clark**. If you choose a smaller one, the card asks first: **Use it anyway** or **Keep the model I have**.
To stop, press **Disconnect**. The card then says: Disconnected. You're still signed in to Claude or ChatGPT on this computer, but clark won't use it.
Fill in your **Name**, **Alias**, **Email**, **Phone number** and **Organisation**.
Each saves when you leave the box (or press [[Enter]]), with **Undo**.
Your full name goes on every change you make, in each item’s history.

Open **Settings** and find the **People** card. It lists everyone who owns a work item or a milestone. The line above the table says how many people still need details (“8 of 8 people need details”). **Show only these** lists just those people, each marked **Needs details**; **Show everyone** brings the rest back.

Press **Paste from Excel**, then paste rows copied from a sheet: name, email, organisation and role, separated by tabs. A first row of headings is skipped. A preview shows what happens to each row, and names every row that needs fixing.
Press **Add to the list**. People are matched by name, so the owner pickers keep working on names. One **Undo**, in the card, takes the whole paste back.
tasks.n: The table is read-only apart from the paste.

tasks.w: The message at the foot of the page · the peek’s history
s: Every change shows a message at the foot of the page with **Undo**, for about 20 seconds. Press **Undo** and the change goes back.
A step of several changes goes back as one, such as **Add from your project record**.
In Edit, the peek’s **Activity** tab shows each change to the item: who made it, how, what it was, what it became, and when.

To take back several changes at once, tick them in the **Activity** tab (click, [[Mod]] and click, or [[Shift]] and click for a run), then press **Undo** with the number. It shows what will go back and what stays, and asks again above 25. **Clear** or [[Esc]] drops the choice.
In an editor, the **Undo** button or [[Mod+Z]] steps back through your typing. [[Esc]] cancels the whole edit.
Open [Settings](go:settings#update) and find **Version and updates**. **Installed** is the version you have now.

From the clark releases page, download the update attached to the release for your computer. If it is in Downloads, **Update** shows **Review X.Y.Z**; otherwise press **Choose zip…** under **Install from a file** and pick the update.
Read the review: the version change, the release notes, the files replaced, added and removed. Your projects, settings and published reports are kept, and a copy of your data is made first.
Press **Install**. The new version starts by itself and the page reloads.
To go back, press **Undo update** in the **Last update** row, then press it again within five seconds. More in [Updating clark](#ref-updating-clark).

tasks.t: Start, check or restore from Terminal (Mac)
s: The download unzips into one folder called clark, whatever its version. Only the zip file keeps the version in its name.

To start clark, double-click clark.command in that folder. Or open Terminal, type cd and a space, drag the clark folder into the Terminal window, press Return, then type `bash clark.command` and press Return.

To check that this Mac is ready, type `bash clark.command --check` in the same place. It prints a line for each thing clark needs, says what to fix, and ends by saying everything is ready or how many things to fix. It changes nothing.
To list the backups, close clark first, then type `bash clark.command restore`. With no name after restore it only lists them.
To put one back, close clark first and add the backup’s name after restore, as the list shows it, for example `bash clark.command restore clark-20261028T143005Z-undo.db`.

What Docker does here. These steps are for a Mac, and you only need Docker and Chrome. If your Mac will not open clark.command (a work Mac often will not), or you already use Docker, use Docker instead. It replaces the Terminal window that runs clark's web server. You open localhost:8766 in Chrome and see clark, as before. Only the web server runs in Docker. Your project data and clark's own files stay in folders on your computer, shared into Docker. The first start downloads a stock Python image once and keeps it; nothing of clark is in it. Nothing else is installed. It can only be reached from this computer: another device is told "This connection was refused" and that clark is running in Docker and only answers this computer.

Before the first start. Install Docker Desktop and open it first. Wait until it says it is running. If you start clark before that, Terminal says it cannot connect to the Docker API: open Docker Desktop, wait, and type the command again.

Use the clark download. Start clark from the download (the zip file), not from a copy of the source code. A copy of the source has no built pages, and clark is shared into Docker read-only, so it cannot build them: it will say that the page could not be built. The message is: "This copy of clark has no built page. Use the clark download, not a copy of the source code." Docker then stops.

Start. Every command below must be typed inside the clark folder: first cd into it. Open Terminal, type cd and a space, drag the unzipped clark folder into the Terminal window and press Return. Then type `docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d` and press Return. The first time takes a few minutes. Then open localhost:8766 in Chrome. This start keeps its data in ~/Library/Application Support/clark, the same place clark.command uses, so you see the projects you already have, or an empty set on a first start. The Dashboard then says "No project open" and "There are no projects yet." Your data is not in the clark folder, so you can swap that folder for a newer download. If you already have a folder called clark, rename or move it before you unzip a newer download, so the two do not clash.

Never use two routes on the same data at once. Stop clark in Docker before you use clark.command, and stop clark.command's window before you start Docker. Neither route can always tell that the other is already using the folder.

Use another data folder. To keep your data somewhere else, put its full path in quotes in front of the command: `CLARK_DATA_DIR="/full/path" docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d`. Use the same line every time you start. A folder inside OneDrive cannot be used by clark. If you used Docker before and your data is in a data folder inside the old clark folder, stop clark, move that folder out of it, and name it this way.

Change the port. Put a port number in front of the start command, for example `CLARK_PORT=8800 docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml up -d`, then open localhost:8800. It is still reachable only from this computer.

Stop. In the same folder, type `docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml down` and press Return. Docker does not stop clark by itself: it keeps running until you stop it this way, even when you close every clark window.
See what clark is doing. To see what Docker has said, type this in the same folder: `docker compose -f docker/compose.yaml logs --tail 50`
If the page will not open. Check that Docker Desktop says it is running. Check that the address is exactly localhost:8766 (or your own port).
If it says port 8766 is already used. Another clark is open: close it, or stop it with the Stop line above, then try again.
If it says it cannot connect to Docker. Docker Desktop is not running yet. Open it and wait until it says it is running.

If an installed clark window says clark is not running. The window is titled "Start clark to use this window" and says: "Nothing is running at this address. Start it the way you started it: double-click clark.command in your clark folder, or, if you use Docker, open Terminal in that folder and type:" then the start command, then "Closing the last clark window stops clark after a minute. Docker keeps running until you stop it with:" and the stop command, and a button Check again. With Docker, type the start command and choose Check again.

To go back to clark.command. Stop clark with the Stop line above, then double-click clark.command in the same folder. Docker and clark.command use the same data unless you name another folder with CLARK_DATA_DIR. If clark.command looks empty, you started Docker with another folder.

b: **The project name**: switch projects. Each shows its count of open items; **Project settings** is at the foot.
**The profile circle**: a person icon at the top right that opens the menu. See [The profile circle](#ref-profile-circle).

The magnifying glass opens **Go to or do**, the same box as [[Mod+K]]. Type to find a command (Publish, Preview the page in a new tab, Export to Excel, Settings, ask clark, Help or Appearance), a page, a project, a work item or a milestone, then press [[Enter]]. A published file has no such button.
At the top right. Its menu has your name and email at the top, then:
**Publish…**: the Publish box, on the Dashboard.
**Preview the page in a new tab**: the page as the client will see it. Nothing is saved.
**Export to Excel**: the whole project as one workbook.
**Export to Word**: the report saved as a Word file, without publishing the web page.
**Import from Word**: reads a Word file and lists the new actions, risks, issues and decisions it found.
**Published reports**: the **Published reports** card in Settings for the open project.
**Appearance**: System, Light or Dark; the one in use has a tick.
**Settings**. Until you add your name in Settings, the top line is a link to Settings and this entry is left out.
**Help**: opens Help for the page you are on, with a link to all of Help.
Publish, Preview and Export appear once the report has loaded.

sections.w: The report, in View or Edit
b: **View** and **Edit**: View shows the report as the client will read it. Edit changes it in place; each change saves on its own.
**Week ending**: the date on the cover, and in the published file’s name.
The line beside it: while you edit, that each change saves on its own; otherwise “Published” on its date, to the client (or locally), or “Draft · not published yet”.
The cover: the project, then “WEEKLY REPORT · Week ending …” and who it is for.
A single click on a work item row, outside its fields, opens it in the peek. The owner, status, priority and due date change in place, in View or Edit; in Edit every part of the row does.

At the right edge, **On this page** is a quiet line for each section; the current one is longer and darker, and a warm one needs a look. Point at it, or tab to it, for the list with counts (late, red, slipped, flagged, pending) and **Back to top**. In a narrow window the lines become an **On this page** button at the bottom right; press it for the same list.
Project health with its reason, and the count tiles.
A strip of counts, then a row per use case that opens in place.
The timeline or calendar, the legend and the list of milestones.
Text sections. This week and Next week sit side by side to start with; any section can sit beside another.
Added from a template: what you need from the client, as rows you add yourself. Left out of the published page when no row is shown. See [Needs from you](#ref-needs-from-you).
Add more sections from the **+** under any section’s move button, or its menu’s **Add a template below…**. See [Section templates](#ref-section-templates). Rename any heading in Edit.

Ready-made sections you add in Edit from the **+** under a section’s move button, or **Add a template below…** in its menu. In the **Add a section** box you pick one, choose **On its own row** or **Beside** the section above (half width), and press **Add section**. See [Add a section from a template](#howto-add-a-section-from-a-template).
Each template works at the widths shown. A template with nothing in it yet is left out of what the client sees.
Words under a heading, written in clark’s one editor.
A story with a picture: a site visit, a design, a screenshot of the new system.
Three or four numbers with labels and a change since last week.
Three numbers with labels, in wider cards, so a short note fits under the change.
Pictures in a grid, each with a caption.
Anything with rows: a budget line, a cut-over plan, a training schedule.
The risks, actions, issues or decisions you want the reader to see, as cards.
Four shorter cards: good for “this week’s actions” or “decisions needed”.
Live rows from Work items, chosen by a filter: open actions due soon, red risks, decisions needed.
The papers that go with this week’s report.
One thing the reader must see.
Next steps or readiness, ticked off.
What the project needs from the client: decisions, information and dates, each with who it is from and when it is needed by.
A web page shown as a card you write: a dashboard, a news item, a recording.
The state of the project in a few lines, to sit beside another section.
Where the plan stands, in clark’s one editor: headings, lists, links and the AI menu. Starts with two headings to fill in.
The plan as bars on a timeline, from your Gantt lines. Only lines put in the client view show.

A section for what you need from the client: a decision, information or a date. Add it in Edit from the **Add a section** box. You add its rows yourself with **Add a row**; each says what is needed, who it is from and the day it is needed by, and is marked as a decision, information or a date.

A row past its date shows the word **Overdue**, so it does not rely on colour. **Leave out** keeps a row in Edit but off the published page. On the published page the section is a table, and it is left out altogether when no row is shown. See [Ask the client for what you need](#howto-ask-for-what-you-need).

sections.t: Freshness: raised, last reviewed, not reviewed
b: **Raised**: when the item came in, from its first change in the history. Raised and Last reviewed are in the peek of an open action, risk, issue or decision.
**Last reviewed**: the latest change you made by hand. A change made by clark or an Undo does not count.
**Not reviewed in 14 days**: shown at the top of the peek on an open action, risk, issue or decision that has not been reviewed for that long.
To get **Not reviewed in 14 days** or **No owner or no date**, type **is:quiet** or **is:incomplete** in the filter line, or save either as a view.

14 days is the default. To change it for this project, open **Settings**, then **Freshness**, and type a whole number from 1 to 365 in **Not reviewed after (days)**. The note and the filter follow at once.
There is nothing to fill in: Raised, Last reviewed and the Not reviewed note follow from the changes made to each item.
An archived milestone leaves the Milestones list, the counts, the Dashboard and the published page.

**Show archived** on Milestones, with the number of them in brackets, lists the archived ones in muted text, each marked **Archived**, with its agreed date and how many work items are still linked to it. A published file has no such list.
An archived milestone is read-only. Its name opens it, with one **Restore** button. Restore works in View and in Edit, and is one step with **Undo**.
A work item keeps its link to an archived milestone.
On track, At risk or Off track, with the reason
Open actions past their due date, “of n open actions”
Red when any; green when none
Open risks and issues of Urgent or High priority
Red when any is rated Urgent or High; amber when some are open but none is that high; green when none are open
Pending decisions, with the oldest date
Amber when any; green when none

A count opens Work items filtered to it. In Edit: drag or [[Alt+Left]] / [[Alt+Right]] to reorder, the eye to hide, right-click for **Outline colour**: Automatic, Green, Amber, Red or No colour. Decisions needed starts hidden in a new project; show it with the eye in Edit. Project health always shows.
The report is the cover, then the sections, with the contents at the right edge. Choose the style in Settings › Personal; one card is the standard. It is used on the published report too.
Each section is its own card, with a slim gap that shows the page picture.
The same, with more space between the sections.
Slim gaps, and each section title in a grey band, like the Work items groups.
All the sections in one long card.

From the top: the type switch; **Open**, **Closed** and **All** with counts; the saved views with the **Table** and **Board** icons and the **View** menu (Group by and Swimlanes); then the filter line.
A letter for the kind of item (the letters are listed in [Types, statuses and colours](#ref-status-words)), the title, then the ID, use case, milestone and workstream
The date, and Today, Tomorrow, “3 days late” or “In 5 days”
The state in words and colour: in View, the pill; in Edit, the status itself; see [Status words](#ref-status-words)

Whether the client sees the item. Open eye: shown to the client. Crossed-out eye: internal only. It follows the item’s client flag, the hidden list and Sensitive labels together, so an item with a Sensitive label shows crossed out. Select it to turn the item on or off, with **Undo**
Overdue, Due in 7 days, No date, Later
Everyone with an item, and none
Shown to the client, Internal only
Not reviewed in 14 days, No owner or no date. Offered once some item has a date it can count from

The filter line takes a plain word, which finds the items with it in the title or the ID, or field:value, such as status:Open or priority:High,Urgent. A comma means or, a space means and, a - in front means not, no:owner finds the items with no owner, has:owner the items with one, and owner:@me means you. The count at the right reads, for example, 12 of 40, and **Clear filter** (the **×**) empties the line. A published file has a **Search work items** box and a **Filter by** row instead, where each filter can be **is any of** or **is not**, and **Clear all** removes the chips.
Group by: Workstream, Status, Due, Owner, Priority, Milestone, Type and Nothing. The board adds **Swimlanes** (Workstream or Type). See [Group work and use the board](#howto-use-the-board).

Assign to: click the owner. Under Recent are the names used lately in this project, then the people clark holds. Type to search them. If the name is new, the box offers to add it “as a new person”, which puts them on the list of people and assigns them in one step; “Keep the name only” assigns the name alone. “TBC (no one yet)” leaves the item with no one yet, and the owner stays as TBC. Recent names are kept in this browser only, not in Excel or a published file. If the browser will not keep them, there is no Recent list, and everything else works.

Draft email: in Edit, right-click a row, or press [[Shift+F10]] on it, and choose “Draft email to” and the owner’s name. It is greyed when the item has no owner. A window opens with the kind of email, **Update request**, **Chase** or **Decision**, the To and Subject lines, the items to tick, **Reply by**, and the choice to include the latest update on each item. For a chase you also pick **First chase**, **Second chase** or **Firmer chase**. You can edit the wording in the window before you copy it. **Copy as text** copies it as plain text, and “Open in your mail app” opens your mail program with the email ready when it is short enough for a mail link. Mail is never sent by clark. **I sent it** records that you sent it: the history keeps the day, the items and the kind of email, not the wording. It says, for example, Recorded: 2 items marked as sent on, then the date (DD-MM-YYYY), and It is in the history. In View, I sent it is off and the window says “Switch to Edit to change this.”

The right-click menu has a small picture before each entry: Draft email to the owner, “Change status”, “Move due date”, “Change owner”, Hide from the client or Show to the client, “Copy link to this item”, “Copy ID”, **Duplicate** and **Archive**. The picture only helps you find the entry; each one still has its words. The eye entry shows the change it makes: a crossed-out eye for Hide from the client, an eye for Show to the client.

The Milestones screen shows every milestone, internal ones too. Switch between **Timeline** and **Calendar** at the top right. The **Legend** and the list of milestones are below; a milestone that is not shown to the client has the tag **Internal only**.

**Movement** is the switch next to **Plan** at the top: the open milestones against their agreed and forecast dates, with how far after the agreed date each is, what changed and a choice to make. It is never published. See [Deal with a slipped milestone](#howto-handle-a-slipped-milestone).

Its purpose is to help you make the report as accurate as it can be. It works from this project’s data and the source folders listed in Settings. It never reads mail, Teams or calendars. It can suggest changes to work items and to milestones, and a new work item or milestone. It never archives or restores anything, and it never takes one out.

Asking is on from the first start. Nothing is sent until you ask a question, and only while Claude or ChatGPT is connected and signed in on this computer. **Turn off asking** in the **Asking** card in Settings stops it. That card also says where a question goes and which account pays for it.

The suggestions sit in one row above the box (scroll it sideways for the rest): **Check this report**, **What is overdue?**, **Which risks are red?**, **What is the next milestone?**, **Summarise this week**, **Which use cases need attention?**
Type a question and press [[Enter]] to send ([[Shift+Enter]] for a new line). While it works, a short waiting line shows in place of the suggestions, and they come back with the answer.

An answer is plain text. A suggested change comes as a card: nothing is saved until you press **Apply**, and **Undo** takes it back. A change that came from one of your files asks you to tick a box first.
**New chat** starts again; **Close**, [[Esc]] or a click outside closes it.
Drag its left edge to make it wider.

Passwords and keys: a question, or a passage from a source folder, that looks like a password or a key is not sent. A password or key with a name in front of it is not sent when its value looks like one: letters mixed with digits or symbols, or a word in quotes. A plain word with nothing else in it, typed after the name without quotes, is still sent, because clark cannot tell it from an ordinary word. A short mixed value typed after “api key” or “access key” (such as v2beta3) is not sent, on purpose, even when it is not a key. Take any real password out of a question before you send it.

The **ask clark** button shows only while asking is on. With asking off, [[/]] still opens the panel, except while Help is open, and the panel says “Asking is off. Turn it on in Settings.” and has an **Open Settings** link.
A work item opens in the peek, over the page from the right. Everything in it saves as you change it, with **Undo**.
**The top bar**: Close, Across the whole screen, Previous and Next, then the eye, Copy link and **⋯** (Duplicate, Archive).
**The line above the title**: the type, the ID, the project, and Client when it is shown to the client.
**A warning**, when an action is overdue or due on a weekend, with fixes.
**The title**, then **Status**, **Priority**, **Owner** and **Due**, each with its icon in colour: the state’s colour, the priority’s, and the date’s (red when late, amber when due within a week).
**Latest update**, with **Draft**, and the words **Shown to the client** when the item is shown to the client; then when it was last updated.
**Details**: Description, Type, Workstream, Milestone, Use case and Client wording.

**Source** (in Edit): under the details, where the item came from, then by and the name of the person who added it. An item brought in from a Word file reads Word import, then the date (DD-MM-YYYY), the file name and the heading it came under, then by and the name.

**Activity** (in Edit): each change to the item, newest first: who, how and when. How reads, for example, In the peek, By Excel import (plans.xlsx) or By Word import (plan.docx). A change made by a file import also has a line under it, which reads Updated from, then the file name, the date (DD-MM-YYYY) and, after by, the name.
With the peek open, a click on another work item or milestone moves the peek to it. A click anywhere else, or [[Esc]], closes it. Drag the left edge to resize it; a double-click puts it back.
Overdue (red) past its due date; Delayed or Due soon (amber, within 7 days); Open (blue); Closed or Cancelled (grey)
Its colour from its priority: Urgent or High red, Medium amber, Low green
Assumption (this letter waits for the owner to confirm)
Dependency (this letter waits for the owner to confirm)
The letter shows before the title in the Work items table. A risk or issue’s colour follows its priority, which is set from impact and likelihood. Priorities are Urgent, High, Medium and Low.

Only the sheets you tick in **What to import** are read; the others are not read or changed. The Gantt sheet, named after the Gantt tab or Gantt, is read the same way: a row whose ID exists updates that line, and a row without an ID adds a line with the next free ID. Its Days and Status columns are worked out and ignored, and an import never removes a Gantt line. If a row of the Gantt sheet breaks a rule (a bad date, Done over 100, a parent that is not a phase, or more than 500 lines), nothing in the file is imported, and the message gives the rule and the row number; untick the Gantt sheet in **What to import** to import the other sheets. A row with no ID, or with a word in the ID column, adds a new line. When an ID appears twice, the second row is left out. On the Actions, Risks & Issues and Decisions sheets, a Milestone or Use case cell reads “ID: name”; on import only the ID before the first colon counts, so renaming a milestone is not a change. The Milestones and Use cases sheets have an Open work items column that lists the IDs of the open actions, risks and issues and decisions linked to that row; it is worked out for the sheet and never read back. s: This is the weekly report, laid out as the client reads it.
**At a glance** shows the project health and the count tiles; press a count to open Work items filtered to it.
The sections under it are the report’s text and lists, one after another.

context.title: The Dashboard in Edit
s: In Edit you change the report itself: its text, its tiles and its sections.
Add a section from the **Add a section** box, and rename any heading in place.
Your profile circle’s menu has **Publish**, **Export to Word**, **Import from Word** and **Export to Excel**.
