guides.t: Add a section from a template
guides.job: Start a new section from a layout, in the place you choose.

steps.d: On the **Dashboard**, press **Edit**. Each section now has a control at the left of its card: a move button and, under it, a **+**.
Point at the section you want the new one to follow and press its **+**. Or click the move button to open the section’s menu and choose **Add a template below…**.

The **Add a section** box opens with the cursor in **Search templates**. On the left, pick a kind: **All templates**, **Text and pictures**, **Figures**, **Work items**, **Files and links**, **People and dates** or **Notes**. Or type a word to find a template by name.
Choose a template in the list, such as **Key figures, four** or **Callout**. [[Up]] and [[Down]] move through them. The box on the right says what the chosen one is for and what it **Holds**.

Under **Where it goes**, choose **On its own row**, or **Beside** the section above, which gives each of the two half the width. **Beside** is greyed out, with the reason under it, when the template cannot be half width or the section above is not on a row of its own.
Press **Add section**, or press [[Enter]]. Press **Cancel**, or [[Esc]], to close the box and add nothing.

guides.result: The new section sits below the one you chose, with its heading ready to rename. It starts empty, and an empty section is left out of what the client sees until you fill it. One **Undo** takes it away again.

guides.job: Change the order of the report, put two sections side by side, or take parts out.

steps.d: On the **Dashboard**, press **Edit**. Each section has a move button at the left of its card (in the margin on a wide window, inside the card on a narrow one). It is faint until you point at the section or tab to it.

To move a section, drag its move button and drop it. A line between two rows puts it on a row of its own. The cover stays at the top. Without a mouse, focus the button and press [[Alt+Up]] or [[Alt+Down]].
Click the move button, or press [[Enter]] or [[Space]] on it, to open the section’s menu.
To move one step, choose **Move up** or **Move down**. A choice that cannot be used is greyed out, with the reason under it.

To put a section beside another, choose **Place beside the next section**. Each takes half the width, and a row never holds more than two. For a section already in a pair the menu says **Full width** instead; choose it to give the section a row of its own.

To keep a section out of the client’s copy, choose **Leave out of the published page**. It stays in Edit, greyed, with a small eye mark under its **+** and the tag **Left out of the published page**. Choose **Include in the published page** to bring it back.
Every section also has **Delete section** in the menu. It removes the section from the report.

guides.result: Edit shows the sections in their new order, and the published page follows it. A section you left out is greyed in Edit and gone from View and from the published page. **Undo** puts back a move, a section left out or a section removed.

guides.job: Read a workbook into the project, see every change before anything is saved, and choose which to keep.

steps.d: Press your profile circle and choose **Settings**. Find the **Data** card: it has two buttons, **Export workbook** and **Import workbook**. Press **Import workbook**.

The box **Import from Excel** says which sheets can be imported: sheets called Actions, Risks & Issues (or Risks and issues, or RAID), Decisions, Milestones and Use cases. A Gantt sheet is offered in the next box when the workbook has one. A row whose ID exists updates that item, and a row without an ID adds a new one. The columns can be in any order, and only the name or title is needed. If you have no workbook yet, press **Get the template**: your browser saves a workbook with the right sheets and columns, and a line says that your browser has saved the template and gives its name.
Press **Choose a file** and pick an .xlsx workbook of up to 25 MB. A macro workbook (.xlsm) is turned away and nothing is saved; save a copy as an ordinary .xlsx workbook and choose that.

The box **What to import** lists the sheets the workbook has, each with its number of rows, for example Actions (12 rows), the Gantt sheet after the others. They all start ticked. Tick the sheets you want and untick the rest: anything you leave unticked is not read and not changed. **Select all** ticks every sheet and **Clear** unticks them. With no sheet ticked, **Continue** is off. A sheet with more than 2,000 rows shows **more than 2,000 rows**. It is refused whole when you press **Continue**, and the message says so.

The box **Check the import** opens. A line gives the counts: new, updated, refused and not in the workbook (the last two only when there are any). Unchanged rows are left alone. Nothing has been saved yet. It counts only the sheets you ticked.

Read the list under the counts. Each change has a tag and the choice **Accept** or **Reject**: **New** rows will be added, **Changed** rows will update the item already in clark, and a row tagged Not in the workbook would archive its item. A line under a change says what differs. A change that has a problem says why and stays on **Reject**.

Choose **Reject** for any change you do not want; **Accept all** and **Reject all** set every change at once. New and changed rows start on **Accept**, except a change that clashes: a line under it says it changed in clark after the workbook was made, and it starts on **Reject**. Rows tagged Not in the workbook also start on **Reject**. If clark has no record of exporting the workbook, it warns you, and the button reads **Import anyway**.

Press the button at the foot, which reads Import and the number you accepted, such as Import 3 changes. The whole import is one step. The box says what was done. Press **Undo this import** to put the project back as it was before, or **Close** to keep it. The project’s pages then show the new and changed items.

guides.result: The box tells you what was added and updated, the rows you left are untouched, and one press of Undo this import takes the whole import back.

guides.job: Save the project as an Excel workbook, know what is in it, and take changes back in.

steps.d: On **Work items**, press the **Export to Excel** icon in the page header, beside the add button.
Or press your profile circle and choose **Export to Excel**. It gives the same workbook from any screen.
Or choose **Settings** from the profile circle, find the **Data** card and press **Export workbook**. It is the same export again.
Your browser saves one .xlsx file, and a message gives its name. Nothing is sent or published: the file is only on your computer.

Open the file. It opens on the Cover: a title band with the project name, tagged INTERNAL, and under it a line with Weekly report, the week ending and who it is for. Then come the sections the published page shows, in the report’s order: the current state, the At a glance tiles side by side (the health is one of them) and the text sections, with This week and Next week side by side when both have words. A quiet About this export block comes last: when it was exported and by whom, a caution that it shows the project as it was on that date, who to send changes back to, where to make changes, and a note on IDs.

After the Cover come the sheets of rows: Actions, Risks & Issues, Decisions, Milestones and Use cases, and a Gantt sheet when the project has Gantt lines. Each row is one item, with its ID in the first column. A History sheet follows with the record of changes, read only. Changes made on the Cover are ignored.

The workbook includes internal notes and Sensitive items, so never send it to a client. To send changes back, edit the rows on the data sheets, leave every ID as it is, and import the file with **Import workbook**.

guides.result: A single Excel workbook is saved by your browser, opening on a Cover sheet, with one sheet for each kind of work and one row for each item.

guides.job: Check the report, then save the finished copy locally and, if you choose, send it to the client.

steps.d: To look first, press your profile circle and choose **Preview the page in a new tab**. It shows what the client will see, and nothing is saved.

Press your profile circle and choose **Publish…**. The box **Publish the report** opens. The line under its title gives the project, the week ending, the number this publication will have, such as this will be Publication 4, and when and where the last one went.

**Local** is always ticked, and the box says you choose the folder and name in the save window. Tick **To client** to copy it to the client folder as well. With no client folder set, that tick is off and a link takes you to Settings, Publishing to set one.

If you want them, tick **Also a Word document** (a Word copy of the report, saved in the folder last used for this project) and **Also a PDF** (your browser’s print box opens and you choose Save as PDF).

With **To client** ticked, a line says the client will see the page, and the Word report if you ticked it, and only what is shown in View mode. A hidden section or a work item with its eye turned off is not included.

If a work item the client would see still has its placeholder title, such as New action, the box warns you with a count. It does not stop you. To fix it, press **Cancel**, rename the item or turn off its eye, and open **Publish…** again.

Press the button at the foot, which reads **Publish locally**, or **Publish and send to the client** when To client is ticked. A spinner shows while it works. If the file name is taken, the box asks what to do: **Add a number**, **Rename it** or, where it is allowed, **Overwrite the existing file**.
The button turns green and reads Published, with the publication number in brackets, such as Publication 4. The box closes by itself after a moment; you can press the button to close it at once.

guides.result: The button shows a green tick and Published with its publication number. The saved page is the one the client sees, and the next publication gets the next number.

guides.job: Give several open work items to someone else in one step, with one Undo to take it back.

steps.d: Open **Work items**.

Click the filter box, which says **Filter by keyword or by field**, and filter by owner: type owner: and pick the person from the suggestions. The hand-over button only appears while an owner filter is on, and not when the filter is “is not”.
Press **Hand over**, beside the button that adds an item. A tick box appears on each open item, and a bar opens above the list. Closed and archived items are not offered.

Tick the items to give away: click a row, or press Space on it. **All** ticks every item offered, and **None** clears the ticks. The bar counts them, such as “3 of 12 selected”. While you are ticking, the keys for changing an item are switched off.

Type the new person’s name in **Hand over to**. It suggests names from your people list, or the names already in the project if the list is empty. If the name matches no one, a line under the box asks you to check the spelling.

Press **Hand over** in the bar. It stays unavailable, with a line saying why, until you have ticked an item and named a person. Above 25 items a question comes first, such as “Hand over 30 items to Priya?”: press **Change** to go on, or **Cancel** to stop.
To leave without handing anything over, press **Cancel** in the bar, or press Esc.
If you change your mind after handing over, press **Undo** on the message that appears, or press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac). The whole hand over goes back in one step.

guides.result: The bar closes and a message says what was handed over. Any item that could not take the change is left out and named in that message. The items now show their new owner, and **Undo** puts them back with their old owner.

guides.job: Keep a set of filters on Work items under a name, so you can come back to it with one press.

steps.d: Open **Work items**, in View or in Edit. Above the table are the saved views as tabs, and under them the filter line. Click the filter line and type a word or pick a field from the list, then press Enter. Each filter becomes a chip, and the table shows only the items that match. Press the x on a chip to take that filter off.
When the table shows what you want, press **+ New view**, at the end of the tabs.

The view is made at once, with no name asked first. It is called View 1, then View 2, and so on, using the lowest number no other view has. To give it a name of your own, see the steps on renaming below.
The new view appears as a tab, with the number of items it shows beside its name, and it is the open tab. The view is kept in your browser, for this project.

To come back to it later, press its tab. The filter line is set to what you saved. Every project starts with the tabs Open items, Actions, Risks and issues, Decisions and All work items, then Overdue and My actions.

If you change the filter line while a view is open, a small dot shows on its tab, and **Save view** and **Discard changes** appear beside the tabs. Press **Save view** to keep the new filters under the same name, and a message at the foot of the page says View saved with the name. Press **Discard changes** to put the filter line back to what the view had. The small arrow beside the open tab’s name has the same **Save changes**, and **Save as a new view…** keeps the new filters as another view. The five tabs that every project has cannot be saved over, so they have no **Save view**. Use **Save as a new view…** for them. **Discard changes** is there on them too.
To rename a view, open it, press the small arrow beside its name and choose **Rename…**. Type the new name in the box labelled **New name for this view** and press **Save**.

To remove a view you no longer want, open it, press the small arrow and choose **Delete**, then press **Delete** to confirm. A deleted view cannot be brought back. This works for the five starting tabs too.

guides.result: Your view is a tab on Work items with its item count. Pressing it sets the filter line to your saved filters, and a dot on the tab tells you when the line has changes you have not saved.

guides.t: See the Dashboard as it stood on a past day
guides.job: Look at the Dashboard as it stood at the end of a past day, read only, and come back to this week.

steps.d: Open the **Dashboard**. Beside **Week ending** on the report bar there is a drop-down that reads **Published weeks**. It is there in View and in Edit, and only once the project has a publication.
To look at a week you published, pick it from the list. Each line reads like DD-MM-YYYY · Publication 3, newest first. A page that was kept opens in a new browser tab exactly as it was published.
A line that ends in rebuilt has no kept page. Picking it shows the Dashboard as it stood on the day that publication was made, rebuilt from the change history, in this same tab.
To choose any other day, pick **Dashboard as at a day…** at the foot of the list. Settings opens at **Published reports**, and the day box in the **Dashboard as at a day** card is ready for you.
Type the day as DD-MM-YYYY and press **Show**. A day that has not happened yet, or from before the project existed, is turned away with a line saying so. Pick another day.

The Dashboard now shows the project as it stood at the end of that day. A banner at the top reads “You are looking at the dashboard as at” and the day, and under it “Read only · this was not published in this form”. Due dates and overdue marks are worked out as at that day.
The report on this page cannot be changed, and there is no Edit, no Publish and no Help while you look. Look as long as you like: nothing is saved.
Press **Back to now** in the banner. You are back on this week’s Dashboard, read fresh from clark.

guides.result: You have seen the Dashboard as it stood at the end of a past day, and nothing in the project has changed. You are back on this week’s Dashboard.

guides.t: Back up and restore your data
guides.job: See the copies clark keeps of your data, look inside one, and put one back if you need to.

steps.d: Press your profile circle and choose **Settings**, then find the **Backups** card. It says that a copy of your data is kept each day, and before an undo or an import.

Read the line under the title. It gives the date and time of the latest backup, or says there are no backups yet: the first one is made when you save your first change of the day. If the latest copy is damaged, the line says so.

Read the list, newest first. Each row shows the date and time, the kind (Daily, Before an undo, Before an import, Before a change, Before a restore or Before an update) and the size. Under the list, a line says how many backups are kept of each kind; the oldest are removed after that.

To look inside a copy, press **Preview** on its row. A box says when the backup is from and how many projects, work items and milestones it holds, then how many you have now. Nothing is changed by looking.
If the box says the backup is of a different database, it cannot be put back over yours and there is no **Restore** button. Press **Close** to leave it.

To put a copy back, press **Restore** on its row, or on the preview box. The box asks, for example, “Put back the backup from DD-MM-YYYY 09:30? What you have now is kept first.” Your current data is replaced by the copy, so everything you saved after that copy was made is no longer in your pages. Before it swaps, clark keeps a copy of what you have now, and it shows in the list as Before a restore.
Press **Put it back** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to stop with nothing changed. If your data changed after you pressed **Preview**, clark refuses and asks you to look at the backup again.

The page reloads and one line says that the backup was restored and that your data from before is kept in case you need it. There is no Undo button for a restore: to go back, look in the list for the Before a restore copy and put that one back.

guides.result: Your pages show the data from the copy you chose, a line confirms the restore, and a Before a restore copy of the data you had is in the list.

guides.job: Know the minimum requirements of a brand kit: what it must hold, the limits, and how to import one.

steps.d: A brand kit is one zip file. It holds clark-brand.json, which gives the brand's name, id and version and its file list, and the colours and fonts file. A logo and cover pictures are optional. It holds no other files. No file name is required.
Keep to the limits: 50 files, 16 MB the zip, 24 MB unpacked, 5 MB a file. No links or paths outside the kit are allowed.
Press your profile circle and choose **Settings**, then find the **Brands** card.
Press **Choose zip…** and pick the kit, or press **Review the brand in Downloads** to read the newest zip in your Downloads folder.
Read the review. It lists what the kit adds, replaces or removes. Nothing changes yet.
Press **Install** for a new brand, or **Replace** for one already added. Press **Cancel** to stop with nothing changed.
To go back, press **Undo** to put back what the last install, replace or remove changed, or press **Remove** on the brand to return to the default look.

guides.result: The brand's colours, fonts and pictures are used, or a plain sentence says what the kit lacks and nothing was changed.
